chunks: What Muḥammad ibn Yaʿqūb narrated from a number of our companions, from Sahl ibn Ziyād, from Aḥmad ibn Muḥammad, from Ḥammād ibn ʿUthmān, from Yaḥyā al-Azraq, from Abī al-Ḥasan عليه السلام, who said:

I said to him: A man performs saʿy between al-Ṣafā and al-Marwah for three circuits or four, then he urinates; may he complete his saʿy without wudu (ablution)? He said: There is no harm. But if he were to complete his rite with wudu (ablution), that would be more beloved to me.

key_terms.أَشْوَاطٍ: circuits or laps of the ritual saʿy
key_terms.الصَّفَا: al-Ṣafā, one of the two sacred points of saʿy in hajj and ʿumrah
key_terms.الْمَرْوَةِ: al-Marwah, the other sacred point of saʿy in hajj and ʿumrah
key_terms.نُسُكَهُ: his rite or ritual act of worship
key_terms.وُضُوءٍ: wudu (ablution), the ritual purification before certain acts of worship
key_terms.يَبُولُ: urinates, indicating the occurrence of a state requiring renewed wudu (ablution)
key_terms.يَسْعَى: performs saʿy, meaning the ritual walking between al-Ṣafā and al-Marwah

ai.seo_question: Can a person complete saʿy between al-Ṣafā and al-Marwah without wudu (ablution) after using the toilet?
ai.summary: This hadith states that wudu (ablution) is not required for completing the saʿy between al-Ṣafā and al-Marwah after one has urinated during it. However, completing the rite while in a state of wudu (ablution) is described as preferable and more beloved.
